outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 13]
outcomes.modelOutput: {"status":"ANSWERED","claims":[{"text":"The six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.","ref":"r1c2","quote":"When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system"}]}

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making a poor capacity decision can result in paying for expensive idle resources or facing the performance issues of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
With cloud computing, organizations can use only the capacity they need and scale in and out automatically. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation happens when demands exceed a workload's capacity, which is a common cause of failure in on-premises workloads. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
Cloud environments allow monitoring workload demand and automating resource addition or removal to maintain optimal capacity without over- or under-provisioning. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way door decisions are reversible and can utilize a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way door decisions are hard or impossible to reverse, requiring more inspection before they are made. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
Organizations should centralize one-way door decisions that could be irreversible. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]
Two-way door decisions may be made by lower level organizational leaders. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a cloud service that offers a consistent process to review and measure your architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The AWS WA Tool provides recommendations designed to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool assists in reviewing your approach prior to development, workload states before production, and workload states in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) refers to the maximum acceptable delay between the interruption of a service and its restoration. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 680]
This objective determines what an organization defines as an acceptable time window during which the service is unavailable. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
RTO represents a target, or maximum value permitted, for an individual availability-impacting event. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Exponential backoff should be used to retry requests after progressively longer intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter should be introduced to randomize retry intervals and avoid aligning requests into traffic spikes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
A maximum number of retries or maximum elapsed time should be configured to prevent backlog build-up. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should be implemented at only one layer of the application stack to avoid compounding attempts into a retry storm. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Being aware of service quotas and constraints helps customers prevent service degradation or disruption in their AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Unexpectedly reaching a constraint can cause an account's applications or services to be degraded or disrupted. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]
Monitoring and automatically managing service quotas and resource constraints helps proactively reduce failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
Workloads should be monitored for key performance indicators (KPIs) to trigger automation when a threshold is breached. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
KPIs used for this monitoring should measure business value rather than the technical aspects of service operation. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Monitoring KPIs enables automatic notification and tracking of failures, as well as automated recovery processes to work around or repair the failure. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
More sophisticated automation allows for anticipating and remediating failures before they happen. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
Security and compliance is shared between AWS and the customer, commonly differentiated as Security of the Cloud versus Security in the Cloud. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS is responsible for protecting the infrastructure—including hardware, software, networking, and facilities—that runs all AWS Cloud services. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS operates, manages, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customers are responsible for securing their applications, data, and the services they select and use. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 130]
Customers assume responsibility for managing guest operating systems, associated application software, and configuring AWS-provided security group firewalls. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
outcomes.answer:
The recommended approach to secrets management is to follow the guidance of remove, replace, and rotate. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Where credentials are required, long-term credentials should be replaced with temporary or short-term credentials, such as temporary credentials using IAM roles. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Long-lived secrets that cannot be removed or replaced can be stored in a service such as AWS Secrets Manager to be centrally stored, managed, and rotated regularly. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 49]
Application and database credentials should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation established if possible. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
OAuth tokens should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation configured. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
API tokens and keys should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager and rotated automatically if possible. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be allowed to perform the smallest set of actions necessary to complete a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle strikes a balance between usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Operating under the principle of least privilege aids in limiting unintended access and tracking who has access to specific resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
The operational excellence pillar recommends making frequent, small, and reversible changes to workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Combining automated deployment techniques with smaller, incremental changes reduces the blast radius and enables faster reversal in case of failures. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Organizations should have processes established for both successful and unsuccessful workload changes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]
Teams should evaluate the benefits and risks of deploying workload changes and verify governance compliance. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 149]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
A runbook is a documented process used to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are used in cloud operations to reduce risk and achieve desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks serve as codified processes providing consistent outcomes for tasks ranging from onboarding team members to deploying major releases. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are commonly used for routine activities rather than responding to non-routine events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Runbooks can be used to document procedures that provide consistent and prompt responses to well-understood events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be utilized to experiment safely and collect feedback from users. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]

AWS Lambda versions can be leveraged to release a new function version for beta testing. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]
A/B testing is applied to new features in order to validate them using real user feedback. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier for your team by delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Rather than requiring an IT team to learn how to host and run a new technology, organizations can consume the technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Consuming technologies like NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning as cloud services enables teams to focus on product development instead of resource provisioning and management. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: What is mechanical sympathy?
outcomes.answer:
Mechanical sympathy involves understanding how cloud services are consumed and always utilizing the technology approach that aligns with your workload goals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]
For instance, it means considering data access patterns when selecting database or storage approaches for your workload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
AWS Lambda allows failed transactions to be delivered to a dedicated Amazon SQS dead-letter queue on a per-function basis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Within AWS Lambda, Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure can be configured to manage retries and route poison-pill metadata to an Amazon SQS DLQ. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Whenever possible, Step Functions should be used to minimize custom try/catch, back-off, and retry logic in serverless applications, such as saving failed state runs and their state into a DLQ. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: What can be considered to reduce the impact of Lambda cold starts?
outcomes.answer:
Provisioned concurrency initializes a requested number of execution environments so that they are prepared to respond immediately to function invocations. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 67]
Allocating provisioned concurrency prior to an increase in invocations ensures requests are served by initialized instances with very low latency. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 67]
Using scheduled scaling with Application Auto Scaling allows you to increase provisioned concurrency in anticipation of peak traffic. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 67]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS offers integrated service discovery that allows containerized services to discover and connect with each other. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 16]
Amazon ECS creates and manages a registry of service names using the Route 53 Auto Naming API, automatically mapping names to DNS records. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Unified service discovery can be used for Kubernetes-managed services through AWS contributions to the External DNS project. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map provides a service registry for resources such as IPs, URLs, and ARNs, offering an API-based service discovery mechanism. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS App Mesh can be utilized in service-oriented architectures to provide reliable discovery and access of services. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 512]

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer:
Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources consumed, while increasing or decreasing usage based on business requirements. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]
For instance, development and test environments can be stopped when not in use since they are typically used only for eight hours a day during the work week, resulting in potential cost savings of 75%. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Cloud waste happens when resources are created with incorrect sizing or when observed usage patterns deviate from expectations. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Organizations should identify and recoup expenditures associated with cloud waste across deployed resources. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Organizations are advised to follow AWS best practices to decrease waste, or seek assistance from their account team and partner to optimize cloud costs. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Attributing resource costs directly to workloads, individual organizations, or product owners promotes efficient usage behavior and assists in reducing waste. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 37]

outcomes.question: Why does the choice of AWS Region matter for the carbon footprint of a workload?
outcomes.answer:
The choice of Region for a workload significantly affects key performance indicators, including carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]
Placing a workload close to Amazon renewable energy projects or in Regions with low published carbon intensity can help lower the carbon footprint of a cloud workload. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 23]

outcomes.question: What is the shared responsibility model for sustainability?
outcomes.answer:
Environmental sustainability is a shared responsibility between AWS and its customers. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
AWS is responsible for sustainability of the cloud, which includes delivering efficient shared infrastructure, managing water stewardship, and sourcing renewable power. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
Customers hold responsibility for sustainability in the cloud, optimizing their workloads and resource utilization while minimizing required resources. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]

outcomes.question: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery do?
outcomes.answer:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server-hosted applications and server-hosted databases from any source into AWS via block-level replication of the underlying server. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It allows an AWS Cloud Region to serve as a disaster recovery target for workloads hosted on-premises or on another cloud provider. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It can also serve disaster recovery needs for AWS-hosted workloads if those workloads consist solely of EC2-hosted applications and databases rather than RDS. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
The service coordinates and orchestrates the recovery of compute resources during a failover or drill. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
Elastic Disaster Recovery applies the Pilot Light strategy by keeping a copy of data and switched-off resources inside an Amazon VPC staging area. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
If a failover event occurs, the staged resources are utilized to automatically launch a full-capacity deployment within the target Amazon VPC recovery location. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 27]
